backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 to reduce variance and improve stability of the Random Forest.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES

backlog.spec: Increase N_BITS from 2048 to 4096 to provide a larger feature space for the Morgan fingerprints.
backlog.title: Increase N_BITS

backlog.spec: Reduce MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.2 to increase the diversity of features sampled at each split in the Random Forest.
backlog.title: Reduce MAX_FEATURES

backlog.spec: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 5 to prevent the forest from over-fitting to individual outliers in the training set.
backlog.title: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with xgboost.XGBRegressor. Use a high learning rate (0.05) and 500 estimators.
backlog.title: Switch to XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor. Use 500 estimators and a learning rate of 0.05.
backlog.title: Switch to LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with catboost.CatBoostRegressor. Use 500 estimators and suppress verbose output.
backlog.title: Switch to CatBoost

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the train_y values before fitting and use np.expm1 to transform the predictions back to the original scale.
backlog.title: Add log1p transformation

backlog.spec: Use sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler on the target y values (logD) and inverse transform the predictions.

backlog.spec: Increase RADIUS from 2 to 3 to capture larger neighborhood information in the Morgan fingerprints.
backlog.title: Increase Radius

backlog.spec: Use XGBoost with max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, and subsample=0.8 to improve generalization.
backlog.title: XGBoost Hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05, and feature_fraction=0.8.
backlog.title: LightGBM Hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Set max_depth=15 in RandomForestRegressor to prevent overly deep, high-variance trees.

backlog.spec: Change the featurization to use GetCountFingerprint instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy to capture frequency.
backlog.title: Morgan FP counts

backlog.spec: Implement a simple validation split inside fit_predict to use early stopping with XGBoost (if time permits).
backlog.title: XGBoost Early Stopping

backlog.spec: Subtract the mean of the target from the training set and add it back to the predictions to stabilize training.

backlog.spec: In the XGBoost/LightGBM models, set learning_rate=0.01 and increase the number of estimators to 1000.
backlog.title: Decrease Learning Rate

backlog.spec: Concatenate Morgan fingerprints (radius 2) with a second set of Morgan fingerprints (radius 3).
backlog.title: Mixed Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Set MAX_FEATURES to 0.1 for RandomForestRegressor to force more diversity in tree splitting.
backlog.title: Reduce MAX_FEATURES for RF

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor with the 'dart' boosting type to improve generalization of the ensemble.
backlog.title: Use CatBoost DART

backlog.spec: Use the 'feature_fraction' parameter in XGBoost/LightGBM to randomly sample features for each tree.
backlog.title: Subsampling Features

backlog.spec: Discretize the target values into bins, predict the bin, and then use the bin centers as the final prediction.
backlog.title: Target Binning

backlog.spec: Set n_estimators=1000 for XGBoost to ensure sufficient boosting rounds.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Use max_features='sqrt' in RandomForestRegressor instead of a hardcoded float.
backlog.title: Random Forest Max Features

backlog.spec: If the logD values are potentially negative or zero, apply a shift to ensure they are positive before log1p.
backlog.title: Log1p Target Transformation

backlog.spec: Add gamma=1.0 to XGBoost to specify a minimum loss reduction for splitting.
backlog.title: XGBoost Gamma

backlog.spec: Set min_data_in_leaf=20 in LightGBM to prevent overfitting on small clusters of molecules.
backlog.title: LightGBM min_data_in_leaf

backlog.spec: Use GetFingerprintAsNumPy and then apply a density normalization (divide by total bits set).
backlog.title: Morgan FP Bit Count

backlog.spec: Apply a standard scaler to the fingerprint numpy array before feeding into the model.
backlog.title: Standardize Input Features

backlog.spec: Set 'logging_level=!=Debug' and 'calculation_type=Fast' in CatBoostRegressor for speed and stability.
backlog.title: CatBoost silence_log

backlog.spec: Change the RADIUS constant from 2 to 3. This captures larger structural environments around each atom. Since we are already using count fingerprints, this should provide richer local context without a massive increase in feature dimensionality compared to binary bits.
backlog.title: Increase Morgan Radius to 3

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the target values (train_y) before fitting the model, and then use np.expm1 on the predictions to return to the original scale. Since logD can have high variance, this might stabilize the training of the gradient booster.
backlog.title: Add log1p Target Transformation

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 500 to 1000. Given the 10-minute time limit and 15 folds, a larger tree count might allow the model to capture more complex interactions in the Morgan fingerprints, provided the learning rate is adjusted accordingly.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES to 1000

backlog.spec: Reduce LEARNING_RATE to 0.02 and increase N_TREES to 1000. This is a standard 'slow learning' approach for LightGBM which often yields better generalization on small, high-noise datasets.
backlog.title: Decrease Learning Rate with more trees

backlog.spec: Augment the Morgan count fingerprints with a few basic RDKit descriptors like MolWt, MaxAbsFreq, and TPSA. Concatenate these values (as a 1D array) to the fingerprint array before passing them to the regressor.
backlog.title: Add RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: Add 'lambda_l1=0.1' to the LGBMRegressor parameters. This provides L1 regularization to the weights, which can help with the high-dimensionality of the 2048-bit fingerprint space.
backlog.title: LightGBM Regularization: lambda_l1

backlog.spec: Add 'min_data_in_leaf=50' (or another small integer > 1) to the LGBMRegressor. This prevents the model from creating leaves that represent only a handful of molecules, which is a common source of overfitting in small datasets.
backlog.title: LightGBM Regularization: min_data_in_leaf

backlog.spec: Standardize the input features (the count fingerprints) using StandardScaler from scikit-learn before training. Although LightGBM is generally invariant to scale, standardizing the counts might improve the numerical stability of the gradient calculations.
backlog.title: Feature Scaling of Input

backlog.spec: Subtract the mean of train_y from all target values before fitting. This ensures the model is predicting the deviation from the average logD, which can sometimes simplify the optimization landscape for regression tasks.
backlog.title: Target Mean Centering

backlog.spec: Implement a simple ensemble by training three LGBMRegressors with different random seeds and averaging their predictions. This is a 'brute force' way to reduce the noise variance of the 0.0042 sd.
backlog.title: Add Random Forest Ensemble

backlog.spec: Apply a log1p transformation to the target values (train_y) before training and use np.expm1 to convert the predictions back to the original scale. This can help the model handle skewed logD distributions more effectively.
backlog.title: Target Log-Transformation

backlog.spec: Subtract the mean of the training targets from all target values (train_y and the test set) during fit_predict. This centers the target, which often helps gradient boosting methods converge more stably.
backlog.title: Standardize Target Mean

backlog.spec: Train three separate LGBMRegressor models using three different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their predictions. This reduces variance and helps smooth out noise in the loss.
backlog.title: Seed-Bagged LGBM Ensemble

backlog.spec: Include the 166-bit MACCS keys in the feature set by using Chem.DataStruct.GetMACCSKeys(mol) and concatenating them with the Morgan count fingerprints and RDKit descriptors.
backlog.title: Add MACCS Keys

backlog.spec: Expand the RDKit descriptors used to include Descriptors.NumHeavyDosers(mol), Descriptors.NumRotatableBonds(mol), and Descriptors.NumAromatic(mol).
backlog.title: Add Heavy Atom Count and Rotatable Bonds

backlog.spec: Lower the LEARNING_RATE constant to 0.01. To compensate for the slower learning, increase N_TREES to 2000. This is a more granular exploration of the schedule.
backlog.title: Reduce Learning Rate to 0.01

backlog.spec: Set the LightGBM parameter 'feature_fraction' to 0.9. This forces the model to build trees using different subsets of the Morgan fingerprints and descriptors in every iteration.
backlog.title: Increase Feature Fraction

backlog.spec: Add the 'lambda_l2' parameter to the LGBMRegressor, setting it to 1.0. This provides stronger weight decay than the previously tested lambda_l1.
backlog.title: Add L2 Regularization

backlog.spec: Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the concatenated feature set (Morgan fingerprints + descriptors) from the training set and use them to standardize the features of both the training and test sets.
backlog.title: Standardize Input Features

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan fingerprint generation from count fingerprints back to bit vectors (GetBitFingerprintAsNumPy), but increase the N_BITS to 4096 to provide a richer representation.
backlog.title: Use Tanimoto Similarity (Bit Count)

backlog.spec: Replace the current manual descriptor list (MolWt, TPSA, MolLogP) with a more comprehensive set of RDKit descriptors. Specifically, use the `rdkit.Chem.Descriptors` module to collect common physical properties like `MolLogP`, `MolWt`, `TPSA`, `NumHDonors`, `NumHAcceptors`, `NumRotatableBonds`, and `HeavyAtomCount`. Concatenate these with the Morgan count fingerprints and MACCS keys.
backlog.title: Add RDKit Descriptors (Full Set)

backlog.spec: Standardize the target variable `train_y` before training. Calculate the mean and standard deviation of `train_y` in `fit_predict`. Scale the training labels, then use the same mean and std to scale the test set (or simply use the training stats to transform the test set). Predict on the scaled values and then inverse-transform the predictions to the original scale before returning them.
backlog.title: Implement Target Standard Scaling

backlog.spec: Add a `feature_fraction` parameter to the `LGBMRegressor` to introduce stochasticity in feature selection for each tree. Set `feature_fraction=0.8` and ensure `max_features` or `colsample_bytree` is not conflicting. This helps prevent overfitting to high-variance features like specific bits in the Morgan fingerprints.
backlog.title: LightGBM Feature Fraction Tuning

backlog.spec: Instead of just taking the count fingerprint, calculate a normalized version. Since count fingerprints can have large values, divide each bit count by the total number of atoms (or a fixed large number) or apply a square root transformation to the counts to reduce the influence of very large atoms/rings before concatenation.
backlog.title: Implement Tanimoto-like similarity for Morgan Counts

backlog.spec: Since logD values can be negative and we are predicting a property that might have a skewed distribution, apply a transformation to the target `train_y` to make it more normally distributed. However, because logD is already a log-scale property, use `np.log1p(train_y + offset)` where offset ensures all values are positive, or try a simple `train_y - np.mean(train_y)` centering.
backlog.title: Log-Transform Target

backlog.spec: Supplement the Morgan fingerprints with RDKit's `rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.GetTPSA` or others, but specifically look for topological torsion counts and atom pair counts if available. If not easily available, use the existing `Descriptors` set but include `NumHeteroAtoms`, `NumAromatic` atoms, and `NumHydrogenBondDonors`.
backlog.title: Add Topological Torsion and Atom Pair Counts

backlog.spec: The default `min_data_in_leaf` for LightGBM is often 20. Experiment with setting `min_data_in_leaf=50` or `min_data_in_leaf=100` to prevent the model from creating leaves that represent only a few molecules, which can be noisy in a small dataset of 3360 molecules.
backlog.title: Adjust LightGBM `min_data_in_leaf`

backlog.spec: Implement a basic learning rate schedule. Instead of a fixed `LEARNING_RATE=0.05`, use a slightly lower rate like `0.02` and increase `N_TREES` to `2000`. This is often more stable than a high learning rate with fewer trees.
backlog.title: Use Learning Rate Decay

backlog.spec: Add `lambda_l1=0.1` to the `LGBMRegressor` parameters. This introduces Lasso-style regularization on the leaf weights, which can help in feature selection by pushing the weights of less useful fingerprints towards zero.
backlog.title: Add L1 Regularization

backlog.spec: Expand the descriptor set beyond MolWt, TPSA, and MolLogP. Include a wider range of physical and chemical properties such as Hydrogen Bond Donors (HBD), Hydrogen Bond Acceptors (HBA), Rotatable Bond Count, and Heavy Atom Count. Concatenate these onto the Morgan count fingerprint and MACCS keys.
backlog.title: Full RDKit Descriptor Set

backlog.spec: Subtract the mean of the training target (train_y) from the training labels before fitting the model. To ensure the model remains valid for prediction, the same mean value must be subtracted from the test molecules' actual targets during evaluation (though the harness handles this, we only modify the training values here).
backlog.title: Target Mean Centering

backlog.spec: Transform the target values (logD) using np.log1p. Since logD can be negative, we must first shift the targets by their minimum value (y - min(y)) so that all values are non-negative before applying the log1p transformation. The model will predict the transformed value, which must be converted back using expm1(x + min_y) in the return statement.
backlog.title: Log1p Target Transformation

backlog.spec: Add both lambda_l1 and lambda_l2 regularization parameters to the LGBMRegressor. Set lambda_l1 to 0.1 and lambda_l2 to 1.0 to encourage sparsity and prevent any single feature from dominating the split decisions.
backlog.title: L1 and L2 Regularization Mixture

backlog.spec: Add the 'feature_fraction' parameter to the LGBMRegressor. Set it to 0.8. This forces the model to select a random subset of the 4000+ features for each tree, increasing the diversity of the ensemble and reducing overfitting.
backlog.title: Feature Fraction Tuning

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed LEARNING_RATE, implement a basic step decay or a smaller learning rate with more trees. Specifically, set LEARNING_RATE to 0.01 and N_TREES to 2500 to allow the model to converge more smoothly.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay Schedule

backlog.spec: Train three separate LGBMRegressor models using the same hyperparameters but different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2). Average the predictions of these three models for each test molecule to reduce variance.
backlog.title: Seed-Bagged LGBM Ensemble

backlog.spec: The concatenated features (Morgan counts, descriptors, MACCS) have different scales. Use the training set to calculate the mean and standard deviation for each feature column, then scale the training and test features (StandardScaler-style) before passing them to the LGBMRegressor.
backlog.title: Standardize Input Features

backlog.spec: To increase the information density of the fingerprints, replace the standard Morgan count fingerprints with a version where the bits are hashed to a larger space (e.g., 8192 bits) to minimize collisions while maintaining the count-based representation.
backlog.title: Hashed Morgan Counts

incumbent.description: Increase the Morgan fingerprint size from 2048 to 4096 bits by changing the N_BITS constant, giving the count fingerprints a larger feature space.

memo:
Helped: richer chemistry features. Morgan counts instead of bits (0.5954), physchem descriptors MolWt/TPSA/MolLogP (0.5500), MACCS keys (0.5320), and Morgan 4096 bits (0.5209/0.5183, the incumbent, replicated). Moving from random forest to LightGBM also helped (0.7230 to 0.6663).
Did not help: other model families (XGBoost 0.6395, CatBoost 0.6672). Radius 3 (0.6285) and radius 2+3 concatenation (0.6083). Hyperparameter tuning gave gains within noise: 1000 trees 0.5466, learning rate 0.02 0.5490, lambda_l2 0.5318, min_child_samples=50 0.5610. Extra descriptors (heavy atoms, rotatable bonds, aromatic rings) gave 0.5323, no gain.
Next: other feature types, such as atom-pair or topological-torsion counts, and more bits or hashed counts. Try the full RDKit descriptor set. Try a mixed ensemble of different feature sets. Tune last. Replicate gains under 0.005. Check the table first, because many slots were lost to aborts on repeated or inapplicable ideas.
